subproblem.title: Isodiametric normalisation: μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)·μH[n]
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, the Euclidean Hausdorff measure μHE[n] on ℝ^P (Mathlib: μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with c_n = addHaarScalarFactor(volume on ℝⁿ, μH[n])) satisfies μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)·μH[n] as measures (setwise), where ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝⁿ and μH[n] is Mathlib's Hausdorff measure with weight diamⁿ. Equivalently c_n ≤ ω_n/2ⁿ, i.e. Hⁿ = μHE[n] is dominated by Simon's normalisation ω_n(diam/2)ⁿ (Simon Ch. 1, 2.1–2.2).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)) ≤ (unitBallVolume n / 2 ^ n) • (μH[(n : ℝ)] : Measure (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 1, Theorem 2.10 (isodiametric inequality) and the completion of the proof of Theorem 2.9 (book/chapter-01.txt, printed proof 'Proof of 2.10' and 'Completion of the proof of 2.9'), translated to Mathlib's normalisation of μHE. This is the normalisation the parent's step 4(i) (Simon 3.26(1), used through simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure) relies on; that SimonGMT result is not in the import closure of the contract, so the inequality is proved here.
0. Notation. For d ∈ ℕ, μH[d](A) = sup_{δ>0} inf{Σ_j diam(C_j)^d : A ⊆ ⋃_jC_j countable, diam C_j ≤ δ} (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure via mkMetric); μHE[d] := c_d•μH[d] with c_d := addHaarScalarFactor (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) μH[d] ∈ ℝ≥0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), on every metric space. Lᵈ := volume on ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), ω_d = Lᵈ(B_1(0)), Lᵈ(B̄_r(x)) = ω_dr^d (Measure.addHaar_closedBall). It suffices to prove c_d ≤ ω_d/2^d in [0, ∞]: then for every P and every set s ⊆ ℝ^P, μHE[d](s) = c_d·μH[d](s) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d](s).
1. Isodiametric inequality (Simon 2.10): Lᵈ(A) ≤ ω_d(diam A/2)^d for every A ⊆ ℝᵈ. For d = 0, ℝ⁰ is a point, L⁰(A) ≤ 1 = ω_0(diam A/2)^0. Let d ≥ 1.
 1a. Reduction. Lᵈ(A) ≤ Lᵈ(Ā) and diam Ā = diam A, and the claim is trivial if diam A = ∞ or A = ∅; so assume A compact and non-empty.
 1b. Steiner symmetrization. For j ∈ {1, …, d}, H_j := {x : x_j = 0} and ξ ∈ H_j, let A_ξ := {t ∈ ℝ : ξ + te_j ∈ A} (compact) and λ(ξ) := L¹(A_ξ). Define S_j(A) := {ξ + te_j : ξ ∈ H_j, A_ξ ≠ ∅, |t| ≤ λ(ξ)/2}.
 1c. S_j(A) is compact. The set π_j(A) = {ξ : A_ξ ≠ ∅} (projection of A to H_j) is compact. λ is upper semicontinuous on H_j: given ξ and ε > 0 choose an open U ⊆ ℝ with A_ξ ⊆ U and L¹(U) ≤ λ(ξ) + ε, and let O := {η + te_j : η ∈ H_j, t ∈ U}, an open set containing A ∩ (ξ + ℝe_j). If ξ_i → ξ, then eventually A ∩ (ξ_i + ℝe_j) ⊆ O (otherwise points ξ_i + t_ie_j of the compact set A∖O would have, along a subsequence, a limit ξ + te_j ∈ A∖O, although t ∈ A_ξ ⊆ U), so A_{ξ_i} ⊆ U and λ(ξ_i) ≤ λ(ξ) + ε eventually. Hence if ξ_i + t_ie_j ∈ S_j(A) converge to ξ + te_j, then ξ ∈ π_j(A) and |t| = lim|t_i| ≤ limsup λ(ξ_i)/2 ≤ λ(ξ)/2: S_j(A) is closed; it is bounded since λ ≤ diam A and π_j(A) is bounded.
 1d. Lᵈ(S_j(A)) = Lᵈ(A). Identify ℝᵈ = H_j × ℝ measure-preservingly (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) ≅ Fin d → ℝ via PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, then split off the j-th coordinate via volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove). λ is Borel (upper semicontinuous). By Tonelli, Lᵈ(S_j(A)) = ∫_{H_j}L¹(S_j(A)_ξ)dξ = ∫_{π_j(A)}λ(ξ)dξ = ∫_{H_j}L¹(A_ξ)dξ = Lᵈ(A), because S_j(A)_ξ = [−λ(ξ)/2, λ(ξ)/2] has length λ(ξ) for ξ ∈ π_j(A) and is empty otherwise.
 1e. diam S_j(A) ≤ diam A. Let x = ξ + se_j, y = η + te_j ∈ S_j(A); a_ξ := min A_ξ, b_ξ := max A_ξ, a_η, b_η likewise. Then λ(ξ) ≤ b_ξ − a_ξ, λ(η) ≤ b_η − a_η, so |s − t| ≤ (λ(ξ) + λ(η))/2 ≤ ((b_η − a_ξ) + (b_ξ − a_η))/2 ≤ m := max(b_η − a_ξ, b_ξ − a_η) (note m ≥ 0). If m = b_η − a_ξ, the points ξ + a_ξe_j and η + b_ηe_j of A are at distance (|ξ − η|² + m²)^{1/2} ≥ (|ξ − η|² + |s − t|²)^{1/2} = |x − y| (as ξ − η ⊥ e_j); the other case is symmetric. Hence |x − y| ≤ diam A.
 1f. Symmetries. S_j(A) is symmetric under the reflection R_j in H_j by construction. If i ≠ j and A is R_i-symmetric, then A_{R_iξ} = A_ξ (R_i commutes with translation along e_j), so λ(R_iξ) = λ(ξ) and S_j(A) is R_i-symmetric.
 1g. Conclusion of 2.10. Ã := S_d(S_{d−1}(⋯S_1(A)⋯)) is compact with Lᵈ(Ã) = Lᵈ(A) and diam Ã ≤ diam A (1c–1e), and symmetric under every R_i (1f), hence under x ↦ −x = R_1⋯R_d x. For x ∈ Ã also −x ∈ Ã, so 2|x| ≤ diam Ã ≤ diam A: Ã ⊆ B̄_{diam A/2}(0), and Lᵈ(A) = Lᵈ(Ã) ≤ ω_d(diam A/2)^d.
2. Lᵈ ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d] on ℝᵈ (Simon's 'completion of the proof of 2.9'). Let A ⊆ ℝᵈ, δ > 0 and (C_j) a countable cover of A with diam C_j ≤ δ. By countable subadditivity and step 1, Lᵈ(A) ≤ Σ_jLᵈ(C_j) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)Σ_jdiam(C_j)^d. Taking the infimum over such covers and the supremum over δ > 0 (the formula of μH[d], Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply; Measure.le_hausdorffMeasure packages exactly this): Lᵈ(A) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)μH[d](A).
3. c_d ≤ ω_d/2^d. μH[d] is an additive Haar measure on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (Mathlib instance isAddHaarMeasure_hausdorffMeasure), so volume = c_d•μH[d] there (Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul; this is how c_d is defined). Let K be the unit cube (parallelepiped of the standard orthonormal basis), with volume(K) = 1 (OrthonormalBasis.volume_parallelepiped); 0 < μH[d](K) < ∞ since μH[d] is a Haar measure and K is compact with non-empty interior. By step 2, c_d·μH[d](K) = volume(K) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)μH[d](K); dividing by μH[d](K) ∈ (0, ∞) gives c_d ≤ ω_d/2^d.
4. Conclusion. For every P and every s ⊆ ℝ^P: μHE[d](s) = c_d·μH[d](s) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d](s), i.e. μHE[d] ≤ (ω_d/2^d)•μH[d] on Euclid P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Steiner symmetrization preserves compactness and Lebesgue measure and does not increase diameter; d symmetrizations give a centrally symmetric set inside the ball of radius diam/2 (Simon 2.10).
Countable subadditivity plus the isodiametric inequality give volume ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n] on ℝⁿ.
Comparing the Haar measures volume = c_n•μH[n] on the unit cube gives c_n ≤ ω_n/2ⁿ, hence μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n] on every ℝ^P.

audit.reason: The proof establishes compactness, volume preservation, diameter control and retained coordinate symmetries under Steiner symmetrization. Covering estimates and Haar normalization then give the exact measure inequality, including dimension zero. This agrees with [Simon, Theorem 2.10](https://web.stanford.edu/class/math285/ts-gmt.pdf) and supplies the normalization needed by good_points.
